Alistar.watch: Watch for Alistar W Headbutt closing the gap into Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar E Trample for a chain of crowd control. Heimerdinger has no mobility, so it’s easy to get hit repeatedly once caught. Keep your distance while Alistar W Headbutt is available. Under your allied turret, don’t give Alistar room to flank and knock you toward the inner side of the turret.
Alistar.build: Alistar deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Use Null-Magic Mantle to survive early, and choose Mercury's Treads. If Alistar P Triumphant Roar lets him sustain, consider Morellonomicon. If you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Alistar.fight: Close the gap and counterattack right after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are used. When fighting again, target the damage dealer behind Alistar.
Alistar.laning: Once Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are used, push the lane or reposition while they’re unavailable.
Alistar.combo: While your turrets are firing, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target. Auto-attack your target to direct turret fire onto them.
Alistar.escape: The moment Alistar W Headbutt is used is your chance to engage.
Alistar.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that move around, so decide in advance where to fight.

Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don’t stand with a wall behind you or in a line with an ally or minion. Bard E Magical Journey can bring him in from the flank, so watch his approach routes. Wait to attack while Bard R Tempered Fate makes its targets immune to damage.
Bard.combo: Then, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on Bard. Auto-attack Bard to direct turret fire onto him.
Bard.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up with moving skirmishes, so pull the fight to a position you chose in advance.
Bard.build: Early on, start with a Null-Magic Mantle to survive, then get Mercury's Treads. Bard deals mostly magic damage, and you need to prepare for being focused after Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns you. If the healing from Bard W Caretaker's Shrine offsets your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Bard.escape: The moment after you force Bard to use Bard E Magical Journey is your window to engage.
Bard.laning: If Bard W Caretaker's Shrine appears in lane, step on it to destroy it.

Brand.watch: Brand P Blaze stacks when he lands abilities in succession, then explodes, so dodge his first ability. If you’re ablaze, move out of the line of Brand Q Sear or hide behind a minion. Even after dodging Brand W Pillar of Flame, watch out for Brand E Conflagration spreading near burning minions.
Brand.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first early, and choose Mercury's Treads. Brand deals mostly magic damage, and Heimerdinger has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Brand.fight: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is used, try to trade near your pre-positioned turrets. First check whether you’re ablaze so you can avoid the stun from Brand Q Sear.
Brand.laning: Don’t place turrets far away. Set them where you’ll stand or along the path your opponent will take, and keep one charge in reserve. Don’t last-hit beside minions Brand has set ablaze; step to the side of the wave.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so when Brand W Pillar of Flame is used and you’re not ablaze, you have a chance to close the gap. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear first, then engage.
Brand.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up if you fight on the move, so decide in advance where to fight.
Brand.teamfight: Place and charge your turrets in a narrow path near an objective or by an allied turret, then let Brand walk into their range. Keep your distance from allies so Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm don’t spread to them. Move farther away when you see Brand R Pyroclasm being cast.

Blitzcrank.watch: If Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls you in, Blitzcrank E Power Fist and Blitzcrank R Static Field can easily follow up. Stand behind minions, and stay well away from bushes when you lack vision of them. When Blitzcrank W Overdrive lets him close in, create distance first.
Blitzcrank.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field deal mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Magic resistance does not block the physical damage from Blitzcrank E Power Fist.
Blitzcrank.fight: Trade right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses or when his mana is depleted. Blitzcrank P Mana Barrier may activate, so secure a way to finish him off before focusing your attacks.
Blitzcrank.laning: Don't stand beside minions; always stand behind them to block the path of Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the late game, turrets can't keep up with fights that move around, so decide where you want to fight in advance.
Blitzcrank.escape: The moment after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses is your window to step forward and trade. Don't engage while crowd control is still available; use the movement speed boost near your turrets to keep your distance.

Braum.watch: If Braum Q Winter's Bite or a basic attack applies a Braum P Concussive Blows mark, move out of range before it stuns you. Don't use projectiles into the front of Braum E Unbreakable while his shield is raised, and dodge to the side of Braum R Glacial Fissure's path when you see its cast animation.
Braum.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first to build magic resistance. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots to prepare for the stun from Braum P Concussive Blows.
Braum.fight: Engage when Braum E Unbreakable ends and Braum W Stand Behind Me is on cooldown.
Braum.laning: Braum Q Winter's Bite only hits the first enemy it encounters, so stand behind minions and avoid clear straight lines between them.
Braum.escape: The moment after you make Braum use Braum W Stand Behind Me is your chance to close the distance.
Braum.phase: If you fight while moving in the late game, your turrets can't keep up, so draw your opponents toward a spot you've chosen in advance.

Hwei.watch: If Hwei E Subject: Torment roots or displaces you, you're likely to get hit by more abilities in quick succession. If Hwei's first ability hits you, move immediately to avoid his second ability and the Hwei P Signature of the Visionary explosion. Don't pass through paths Hwei has covered with ground effects; take a wide detour.
Hwei.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Hwei deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Since Heimerdinger has no mobility ability, also consider tenacity.
Hwei.fight: The moment after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used for poke or waveclear is your chance to fight.
Hwei.laning: Place turrets where you plan to stand and along your retreat path, and keep at least one placement charge available for immediate use during a fight. If you see an eye Hwei has left behind, don't enter along that path; choose another route.
Hwei.combo: Tag Hwei with a basic attack to direct your turrets' damage toward him.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility ability, so close the distance right after he has spent Hwei E Subject: Torment.
Hwei.phase: In the late game, turrets can't keep up with fights that move around, so decide where you want to fight in advance.

Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale knocks enemies up, and when fully charged, its range and knockup duration increase. If you hear a tornado from a bush or out of vision, move out of its path, and be cautious about engaging right after Janna disappears from sight.
Janna.fight: Bait out Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then look for an opening the moment the shield is gone. If you can target someone other than the shielded target, focus your damage on them.
Janna.laning: Poke the ally Janna is protecting to make her use Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then make her waste Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr before taking control.
Janna.combo: Then use a basic attack to mark your target and direct your turrets' damage toward them. To start an engage, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it along Janna's retreat path.
Janna.escape: The moment after Janna Q Howling Gale is used is your chance to close the distance.
Janna.teamfight: If Janna stays behind an allied damage dealer, your engage may be pushed back, so look for a chance to catch her alone with Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! cast on E. If the enemy engages first, stop their advance with E's stun, fall back behind your turrets, and hold your position.
Janna.build: Early on, start with a Null-Magic Mantle to survive, then get Mercury's Treads. Janna deals mostly magic damage, and Heimerdinger has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance if you build resistances. If the healing from Janna R Monsoon keeps the enemy side in the fight, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Janna.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up with fights that move around, so decide where you want to fight in advance.

Lulu.watch: If Lulu W Whimsy hits you, you can’t cast abilities, so don’t close the distance while it’s available. Lulu R Wild Growth saves its target and knocks up nearby enemies, so don’t count on securing a kill on that target while R is available. Watch out for the slow from Lulu Q Glitterlance and keep your distance.
Lulu.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lulu's damage is mostly magic, and Heimerdinger has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Lulu.fight: Close in when Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally. If Lulu E Help, Pix! is used on an ally, target Lulu herself.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the bonus damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion. Place turrets at entrances the enemy may use, such as a brush entrance or river approach. Keep at least one turret charge in reserve to place immediately where a fight breaks out.
Lulu.escape: The chance to close in comes after Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally. If Heimerdinger is caught, interrupt it with E and retreat behind your turrets.
Lulu.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up if you fight while moving, so decide in advance where to fight.
Lulu.teamfight: If Lulu R Wild Growth is available, target Lulu or someone else instead of pouring all your damage into the target she is protecting.
Lulu.combo: Then, while your fully charged turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, and use basic attacks to mark your focus target. When you need to cover a wide area, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it along Lulu's retreat path.

Leona.watch: If Leona E Zenith Blade hits you, she dashes onto you, and stuns from Leona Q Shield of Daybreak and Leona R Solar Flare may follow, so keep your distance preemptively. When Leona W Eclipse is active, move out of its area before it explodes. If Leona R Solar Flare's indicator appears, move sideways to avoid the stun at its center.
Leona.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Leona's damage is mostly magic, and Heimerdinger has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Leona.fight: Counterattack by closing in just after Leona E Zenith Blade is used.
Leona.escape: Just after Leona E Zenith Blade is used, she has spent her gap closer, giving you an opportunity to engage.
Leona.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up with a skirmish that moves around, so decide in advance where to fight.
Leona.teamfight: If Leona P Sunlight marks you, the enemy may follow up with more damage, so retreat immediately. If you need to hold your ground, use a turret empowered by Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!!.

Karma.watch: The area slow from Karma Q Inner Flame is dangerous, and the empowered Q ground effect from Karma R Mantra explodes again after a short delay, so move out of its radius immediately if you’re hit. If Karma W Focused Resolve tethers you, create distance to break the tether before you’re rooted. If allies nearby are shielded by Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra, don’t burst them; wait for the shield to expire.
Karma.build: Since Karma’s main damage is magic, use a Null-Magic Mantle to withstand it early and choose Mercury’s Treads. If the healing from Karma W Focused Resolve empowered by Karma R Mantra helps her stay alive, consider Morellonomicon. If you’re playing support and short on gold, wait until after completing one core item.
Karma.fight: While Karma W Focused Resolve is available, create distance first to bait it out. Fight after the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra expires.
Karma.combo: While your fully charged turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, then use a basic attack on Karma to direct your turrets' fire onto her. If you're starting a teamfight, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it along Karma's retreat path.
Karma.escape: The opportunity to engage comes after you bait out Karma W Focused Resolve and its tether breaks.
Karma.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that move around, so decide in advance where to fight.
Karma.teamfight: If Karma engages first, interrupt her with E and retreat behind your turrets.
Karma.laning: Place a turret on your retreat path too, creating an opportunity to use the movement speed from Heimerdinger P Hextech Affinity to break Karma W Focused Resolve's tether.

Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, you’re likely to get hit by her follow-up abilities, so bait out Q, dodge it, and then move. You can still be rooted as its second target even while standing behind an ally, so don’t line up with them. If the red targeting line from Lux R Final Spark appears, dodge sideways.
Lux.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Lux's magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads, and prioritize magic resistance afterward as well.
Lux.laning: Place turrets where you plan to stand and at entrances such as a brush entrance or river approach. Keep one turret charge for use during a fight. Spread out sideways from your allies to make Lux Q Light Binding easier to dodge.
Lux.combo: Then use a basic attack to mark Lux and direct your turrets’ fire.
Lux.escape: The moment Lux Q Light Binding is used is your chance to close the distance.
Lux.phase: In the late game, your turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that move around, so fight in the spot you chose in advance.
Lux.teamfight: Approach spread out from your allies so you aren’t all caught in Lux E Lucent Singularity.
Lux.fight: Engage from the spot where you set up your turrets, right after dodging Lux Q Light Binding.

Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back and slows the first enemy it hits, so before approaching Milio, dodge this ability first or check that it has already been used. Hold off on front-line fights while Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and extends the enemy marksman's range.
Milio.build: Early on, use a Null-Magic Mantle to withstand Milio’s magic damage, and buy Mercury’s Treads. Consider Morellonomicon once Milio’s healing starts to offset turret damage, but if you’re short on gold as a support, wait until you’ve completed one core item.
Milio.laning: Place turrets at brush entrances or river approaches, and keep at least one charge in reserve. Wear down Milio’s mana with early trades and take control of the wave.
Milio.escape: The moment Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is on cooldown is your chance to approach him. If Milio W Cozy Campfire is extending the enemy marksman’s range, wait until that effect ends before going in.
Milio.phase: Milio’s team gets stronger as the game goes on, so pressure them early with trades and wave control. Later, avoid skirmishes that spread out as players move, and fight where you’ve already set up turrets.
Milio.teamfight: If the enemy engages first, interrupt them with your grenade stun and fall back behind your turrets.
Milio.combo: While your turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, and use basic attacks to mark Milio and direct your turrets' fire onto him.

Morgana.watch: If Morgana Q Dark Binding hits you, Morgana W Tormented Shadow and follow-up attacks will come next, so move with minions between you and her. When low on health, don’t walk through Morgana W Tormented Shadow. If Morgana R Soul Shackles connects, use Heimerdinger P Hextech Affinity’s movement speed to get out of range before the stun triggers.
Morgana.build: Early on, use a Null-Magic Mantle to withstand Morgana’s magic damage, and buy Mercury’s Treads. Consider Morellonomicon if fights drag on because of Morgana P Soul Siphon and Morgana W Tormented Shadow. If you’re short on gold as a support, put it off until you’ve completed one core item.
Morgana.laning: When taking a risky position, place a turret along your retreat path too.
Morgana.combo: Then line up Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets to hit, and auto-attack your focus target to direct your turrets’ fire.
Morgana.escape: Morgana has no ability to create distance on her own, so pressure her into range of your pre-placed turrets and follow up with a stun and damage.
Morgana.phase: Later, turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that spread out as players move, so decide where to fight in advance.

Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison stuns you if it hits, so walk sideways to dodge when you see its tell. Nami R Tidal Wave also travels slowly, but a hit leads to follow-up attacks, so move aside as soon as you see it. Don’t fight head-on against an enemy affected by Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing until the effect ends.
Nami.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Nami deals mostly magic damage and has threatening crowd control, so build magic resistance and tenacity. If Nami W Ebb and Flow’s healing offsets your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon, but if you’re short on gold as a support, wait until you’ve completed one core item.
Nami.laning: After securing vision, look for chances to poke Nami, who is low on health and has no mobility ability.
Nami.escape: The moment Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your chance to go in. If you see Nami R Tidal Wave, dodge sideways first, and wait until Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing expires before fighting an affected enemy.
Nami.phase: Later, turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that spread out as players move, so decide where to fight in advance.

Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line starts his engage and follow-up crowd control, so dodge it with minions between you and him. Nautilus P Staggering Blow roots you with his first basic attack, so don’t stay within his basic attack range. Nautilus R Depth Charge follows its target and knocks up allies along its path, so don’t stand on top of an ally while Nautilus has his ultimate available.
Nautilus.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Nautilus’s main damage is magic, and Heimerdinger’s magic resistance is relatively low, so build magic resistance first.
Nautilus.fight: Trade right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. After the trade, create distance to avoid Nautilus P Staggering Blow.
Nautilus.laning: Keep at least one turret charge in reserve so you can place a turret right where a fight breaks out.
Nautilus.combo: Auto-attack the target you want to catch to direct your turrets’ fire.
Nautilus.escape: The moment Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses is your chance to go in and trade. Before Nautilus Q Dredge Line becomes a threat again, use the movement speed from Heimerdinger P Hextech Affinity near your turrets to create distance.
Nautilus.phase: Later, turrets can’t keep up with skirmishes that spread out as players move, so decide where to fight in advance.
Nautilus.teamfight: When you need to hold your position, use Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on Q to block the passage, and don’t stand on top of an ally in the path of Nautilus R Depth Charge.

Maokai.watch: Maokai W Twisted Advance roots and latches onto you, so while it is ready, stay out of range near brush. Avoid brush with Maokai E Sapling Toss saplings, and if a sapling follows you, lead it toward a minion or monster rather than an ally. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp approaches from far away, move perpendicular to its path.
Maokai.build: Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Maokai's main damage, and get tenacity to deal with his root. Consider Morellonomicon if healing from Maokai P Sap Magic lets him survive trades, but as a support, delay it until after completing one core item if gold is tight.
Maokai.fight: Keep your distance while Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, and look to trade right after his dash ends. Maokai is untargetable during the dash, so don't use basic attacks then. Repeatedly hitting Maokai with abilities brings Maokai P Sap Magic's healing back sooner, so focus your damage on the enemy carry when possible.
Maokai.laning: Even if you place a turret at the brush entrance, don't enter brush with Maokai E Sapling Toss saplings.
Maokai.combo: Follow up with Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets while your fully charged turrets are firing. To start a teamfight, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on your grenade and throw it along the enemy's retreat path. Use a basic attack to mark your focus target and direct your turrets' fire.
Maokai.escape: The moment after you make Maokai use W Twisted Advance is your window to move forward. Don't enter range first while Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready.
Maokai.phase: In late game fights on the move, your turrets can't keep up, so choose where to fight in advance.
Maokai.teamfight: While your allies hold their positions, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on a turret to block an approach, and focus your turrets' fire on the enemy carry.

Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault targets and stuns you, so don't give him the range. When Pantheon Q Comet Spear is poking you, keep a minion between you and him. If you see the landing indicator for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk outside its landing area.
Pantheon.build: Survive the early game with Cloth Armor, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Pantheon's main damage is physical, so build armor first. Avoid choosing an item that only greatly increases your health to deal with Pantheon W Shield Vault. If he often jumps in and you frequently allow him to engage, include Zhonya's Hourglass in your core build order.
Pantheon.fight: Draw Pantheon toward a position where you've already placed turrets, while staying outside Pantheon W Shield Vault's range. When Pantheon uses E Aegis Assault, don't unload your abilities from the front; wait for it to end or angle in from the side.
Pantheon.laning: Save one turret charge so you can place a turret right where Pantheon engages.
Pantheon.combo: While your turrets are firing, concentrate Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets on your target and use a basic attack to mark the target for your turrets.
Pantheon.escape: When Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, you have a chance to engage, but if Pantheon R Grand Starfall is still available, he can use it to escape.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon's influence wanes in the late game, but Heimerdinger is also weak in skirmishes on the move, so choose where to fight in advance.

Pyke.watch: If you're pulled by Pyke Q Bone Skewer, Pyke E Phantom Undertow can follow up with a stun, so keep your distance. If Pyke dashes with E Phantom Undertow, move to the side of the direction he came from to avoid the stun trail. If you see a shark shadow beneath your feet, Pyke W Ghostwater Dive is close, so retreat toward an ally or turret.
Pyke.build: Pyke deals mostly physical damage, and Heimerdinger has low armor, so survive early with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps. If you need time to withstand Pyke's engage, include Zhonya's Hourglass in your core build order. Consider Morellonomicon if Pyke's healing offsets your trades, but as a support, delay it until after completing one core item if gold is tight.
Pyke.laning: When you take a risky position, place turrets along your retreat path too, so you can use the movement speed from Heimerdinger P Hextech Affinity. After trading, maintain vision to prevent healing from Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones.
Pyke.escape: The moment after you dodge Pyke E Phantom Undertow to the side is your chance to counterattack. If only one of Pyke's movement abilities is down, he can escape with the other, so don't rush your engage.
Pyke.phase: In late game fights on the move, your turrets can't keep up, so draw the fight to a position you've chosen in advance.
Pyke.teamfight: Don't stand next to a low-health ally, to avoid both of you being hit by Pyke R Death From Below.
Pyke.combo: Then, while your fully charged turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, and use basic attacks to mark Pyke and direct your turrets' fire onto him. To start a team fight, you can cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it along Pyke's retreat path.

Rell.watch: When Rell E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one ally together, an engage is imminent. Stop trading and move beyond the short range of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down. Rell Q Shattering Strike comes in a straight line, so dodge sideways. Keep your distance from allies so Rell R Magnet Storm cannot pull several of you in.
Rell.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early to help you survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rell deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first.
Rell.fight: Whittle down Rell's health with magic damage from outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range.
Rell.laning: Rell has low magic resistance early and cannot recover health in lane, so keep poking from outside her engage range.
Rell.combo: Then use basic attacks to mark a target and direct your turrets' fire.
Rell.escape: When Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is her only ability on cooldown, Rell can escape with Rell E Full Tilt, so don't rush in.
Rell.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up with a moving skirmish, so draw fights to a spot you've chosen in advance.

Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance knocks you up at its landing point, so sidestep as soon as the dash begins.
Rakan.build: Rakan deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If healing from Rakan Q Gleaming Quill provides sustain during trades, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Rakan.fight: Trade right after Rakan P Fey Feathers' shield is stripped away. Rakan E Battle Dance can only be cast on allied champions, so an isolated Rakan can be a target.
Rakan.escape: The moment after Rakan W Grand Entrance is used is your chance to engage.
Rakan.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up with a moving skirmish, so choose your fighting spot in advance.

Renata.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Renata Glasc deals mostly magic damage, and Heimerdinger has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If healing from Renata Glasc W Bailout is making it possible to hold out, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Renata.laning: Dodge Renata Glasc E Loyalty Program sideways, and poke Renata Glasc herself, since she has no mobility ability.
Renata.combo: When your fully charged turrets are firing, line up Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets to hit, then use basic attacks to mark Renata Glasc and direct your turrets' fire.
Renata.escape: After crowd control such as Renata Glasc Q Handshake is used, that's your chance to close the distance.
Renata.phase: In the late game, Heimerdinger's turrets can't keep up with a moving skirmish, so fight from a spot you've chosen in advance.
Renata.teamfight: If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is ready, keep your distance from allies as you engage.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots the first target hit and can stun allies when that target is thrown into them, so dodge it from behind minions or your frontline. Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover makes you attack nearby allies if it hits you, so keep your distance from them while this ability is ready. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, retreat with your allies so they can’t fully revive through a takedown.

Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness passes through allies and minions, so move out of the line between Senna and her target. Senna W Last Embrace has a delay before it roots after hitting, so dodge from behind minions; if you're marked, move away from allies. If Senna hits you once, retreat immediately so she can't hit you again and gain Mist.
Senna.build: Senna's main damage is physical, and Heimerdinger has low armor, so build armor first. Buy Cloth Armor early to help you survive, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. If healing from Senna Q Piercing Darkness offsets your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Senna.fight: Senna is also vulnerable to poke when she steps forward to collect a soul.
Senna.laning: Place turrets at brush entrances or river approaches rather than in the middle of the lane, and save at least one placement charge for a fight. When a soul appears, watch where Senna will come out, take position in advance, and poke her to stop her from collecting it. Stay out of the line of Senna Q Piercing Darkness, but stand behind minions so you can dodge Senna W Last Embrace.
Senna.combo: While your turrets are firing, line up Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets to hit, then use basic attacks to mark Senna and direct your turrets' fire.
Senna.escape: After Senna W Last Embrace is used, that's your chance to close the distance.
Senna.phase: In the late game, Senna's attack range and attack damage grow, while Heimerdinger becomes less effective in moving skirmishes, so choose your fighting spot in advance.

Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed targets and stuns immobilized targets. If you get slowed, move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. In teamfights, Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits an ally, so don't stand in a line.
Seraphine.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads. Seraphine deals mostly magic damage, and Heimerdinger has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If healing from Seraphine W Surround Sound offsets your turret damage and provides sustain, consider Morellonomicon; if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Seraphine.fight: Right after dodging Seraphine E Beat Drop is your chance to close the gap and trade damage.
Seraphine.laning: Place turrets where Seraphine is likely to enter, such as at a brush entrance or river approach, rather than in the middle of the lane, and save at least one turret charge for a fight. Her catch ability can make it easy for her to land follow-up attacks, so manage your distance and don't stray too far from your turrets.
Seraphine.phase: In the late game, turrets can't keep up with fights that move around, so decide where to fight in advance.
Seraphine.teamfight: Place and charge turrets in a narrow passage near an objective or near an allied turret, then make Seraphine come into their range. Spread out to either side of your allies to avoid Seraphine R Encore hitting you in succession.
Seraphine.combo: Then, while your fully charged turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, and use a basic attack on your chosen target to direct your turrets’ fire onto it. When you need to cover Seraphine’s retreat path, cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it toward that path.
Seraphine.escape: Seraphine has no mobility ability, so engage right after you avoid Seraphine E Beat Drop. If Heimerdinger is caught instead, use E to stop the engage and retreat behind your turrets.

Soraka.watch: If Soraka Q Starcall hits, Soraka heals and gains movement speed, so dodge it if you want to keep up the pressure. Inside Soraka E Equinox's area, you are silenced and may be rooted, so move clear before stepping into it. Keep Soraka R Wish in mind when looking for a kill, since it also heals allies in other lanes.
Soraka.build: Early on, withstand her damage with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads. Soraka deals magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If her healing offsets your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon; if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Soraka.fight: Once Soraka E Equinox is down, place turrets where you plan to fight and go in. Pressure the enemy marksman first to make Soraka use Soraka W Astral Infusion, which lowers Soraka's health. Keep pressuring while dodging Soraka Q Starcall, and if you get a chance to take down Soraka, focus your damage on her rather than on one of her allies receiving her healing.
Soraka.laning: Place turrets where the enemy is likely to enter, such as at a brush entrance or river approach, rather than in the middle of the lane, and save at least one turret charge for a fight.
Soraka.combo: When starting a teamfight, you can cast Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! on E and throw it toward Soraka's retreat route.
Soraka.escape: The moment Soraka E Equinox is used to poke and goes on cooldown is your chance to go in. Soraka has no mobility ability, so after closing the gap, keep attacking from a position where your turrets are ready.
Soraka.phase: In the late game, turrets lose their strength in fights that move around, so decide where to fight in advance.
Soraka.teamfight: If you can target Soraka, focus your damage on her instead of continuing to attack one of her allies receiving her healing.

Sona.watch: When Sona moves forward, watch for Sona R Crescendo and don't stand in a line with your allies. After Sona has used basic abilities several times, if she comes within basic attack range, expect an empowered attack from Sona P Power Chord and create distance.
Sona.build: Early on, withstand Sona's magic damage with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads. If the healing from Sona W Aria of Perseverance offsets your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon; if you're short on gold as a support, get it after completing one core item.
Sona.laning: Place turrets at a brush entrance or river approach rather than in the middle of the lane, and save one turret charge. If you keep trading early, Sona will try to endure with Sona W Aria of Perseverance and run out of mana first.
Sona.escape: Your chance to go in is after Sona R Crescendo is down and before she uses Sona E Song of Celerity to gain movement speed.
Sona.phase: Early on, Sona has low health and attack damage, and Sona P Power Chord hasn't built up stacks, so press your advantage then. In the late game, Sona's scaling and sustained healing become strong, and turrets can't keep up with fights that move around, so decide where to fight first.
Sona.combo: While your turrets fire, aim Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets so the rockets converge on your target, and use a basic attack on Sona to direct your turrets’ fire onto her. If Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, throw an empowered grenade along Sona’s retreat path and try to stun her.
Sona.teamfight: When Sona moves close to one of her allies to share her aura, throw a grenade empowered by Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! along her escape route to disrupt her positioning. Spread out laterally from your allies to avoid getting hit together by Sona R Crescendo.

Taric.watch: Dodge Taric E Dazzle by watching for the tell and moving sideways. When Taric R Cosmic Radiance grants damage immunity, stop attacking and manage your positioning until it ends.
Taric.build: Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Taric's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. If Taric Q Starlight's Touch heals through your turret damage, consider Morellonomicon, but if you're short on gold as a support, delay it until after completing one core item.
Taric.fight: After dodging Taric E Dazzle, keep your range and poke. Rather than trading into Taric P Bravado's empowered basic attacks, create distance to limit his chances to attack.
Taric.laning: Place turrets at brush entrances or river approaches rather than in the middle of the lane, and keep at least one charge in reserve.
Taric.combo: Basic attack your intended target to direct your turrets' fire. If you need a wide-area stun, empower Heimerdinger E with Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!!.
Taric.escape: Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so the window after Taric E Dazzle is used is your chance to move forward. If things get dangerous, retreat near turrets you placed behind you and use the movement speed from Heimerdinger P Hextech Affinity.
Taric.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up with fights that break out on the move, so draw fights to a position you chose in advance.
Taric.teamfight: Set up and charge turrets in advance in a narrow passage in front of an objective to make Taric's team come to you. If they engage, interrupt them with E and retreat behind your turrets. When you need to hold your position, empower Heimerdinger Q with Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! to block the passage.

Thresh.watch: If Thresh Q Death Sentence catches you, Heimerdinger has no ability to escape on his own, so follow-up hits are likely. Move sideways when Thresh raises his hook, and change direction once more when moving forward. Avoid the line between Thresh and his allies so Thresh E Flay doesn't pull you toward them.
Thresh.build: Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance against the magic damage from Thresh's main abilities, but prioritize tenacity because Heimerdinger has no mobility and is easy to catch.
Thresh.fight: When Thresh steps forward to collect souls, trade from a position where you have turrets. Hit your intended target with a basic attack or ability first to focus your turrets' fire.
Thresh.laning: Keep at least one charge in reserve so you can place a turret right where a fight breaks out, and set up turrets along your retreat path as well.
Thresh.combo: While your turrets fire, line up Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets and hit your target, then use a basic attack to mark who to focus. When starting a major fight, empower Heimerdinger E with Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! and throw it along Thresh's retreat path.
Thresh.escape: The moment after you dodge Thresh Q Death Sentence sideways is your chance to close the gap. Don't move in first where Thresh E Flay could pull you in.
Thresh.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up with fights that break out on the move, so choose where to fight in advance.
Thresh.teamfight: Place and charge turrets in a narrow passage in front of an objective or near an allied turret to prepare a spot for Thresh to enter. If Thresh R The Box traps you, immediately choose which wall to break through. If Thresh W Dark Passage is thrown, use your finishing ability at once or retreat.

Velkoz.watch: Vel'Koz Q Plasma Fission hits both sides after splitting, so even if you dodge the initial projectile, don't just move sideways; move toward Vel'Koz or back into the area the beam has already passed through. If you're knocked up by Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption and then hit by consecutive abilities, Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction can trigger its true damage, so retreat when stacks have built up.
Velkoz.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Vel'Koz's main ability damage, but Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction and Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray deal true damage that resistance can't block, so move to avoid being hit repeatedly.
Velkoz.fight: Vel'Koz has no mobility, so close the gap and fight during this window.
Velkoz.laning: If you've been hit by consecutive Vel'Koz abilities and stacks have built up, retreat and let them fade. Clear vision around the river and tri-brush to make it harder for Vel'Koz to step forward and poke.
Velkoz.combo: Then basic attack Vel'Koz to direct your turrets' fire.
Velkoz.escape: Vel'Koz has no mobility, so the moment after Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses is your chance to engage.
Velkoz.phase: In the late game, Heimerdinger's turrets can't keep up with fights that break out on the move, so choose where to fight first.
Velkoz.teamfight: If they engage, interrupt them with your grenade and retreat behind your turrets. When you need to hold your position, block the passage with turrets empowered by Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!!.

Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charging, change direction and dodge well to the side. If Xerath E Shocking Orb stuns you, you can take the full follow-up combo, so be especially careful of that shot. Move immediately to dodge when you see Xerath R Rite of the Arcane's cast animation.
Xerath.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Most of Xerath's damage is magic, and Heimerdinger has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance.
Xerath.fight: While Xerath charges Q Arcanopulse, dodge to the side and close the distance. Damage Xerath first to draw your turrets' attacks onto him.
Xerath.laning: Place turrets where Heimerdinger can stand and along the paths the enemy must take to engage, and save one charge so you can place a turret immediately during a fight. Rather than trying to dodge all of Xerath's poke, avoid the heavy damage and farm. When Xerath is running low on mana, push the lane and call your jungler.
Xerath.combo: Follow up with basic attacks on Xerath to draw your turrets' fire onto him.
Xerath.escape: Right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and W Eye of Destruction have been spent is your chance to close the distance. If Xerath is casting R Rite of the Arcane, you can also engage at the spot where he is unable to move.
Xerath.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up if you fight while moving, so fight from a spot you chose in advance.

Zilean.watch: Once Zilean Q Time Bomb attaches, move away from your allies and get outside the blast radius. If Zilean E Time Warp slows you, it becomes difficult to dodge the bomb.
Zilean.build: Early on, withstand Zilean's magic damage with a Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Tenacity pays off early because Zilean Q Time Bomb's stun and Zilean E Time Warp's slow can lock you down. Consider Morellonomicon if the healing from Zilean R Chronoshift provides enough sustain to endure fights, but if you're playing support and short on gold, delay it until after completing one core item.
Zilean.combo: While your fully charged turrets are firing, line up Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets and basic attack Zilean to draw your turrets' fire onto him.
Zilean.phase: In the late game, fight from a spot where you've already placed your turrets instead of taking a moving skirmish.
Zilean.teamfight: If Zilean R Chronoshift is on a damage dealer, switch your target to Zilean himself. Don't use abilities on a target being revived; prepare to act as soon as they revive.

Zyra.watch: If Zyra E Grasping Roots roots you, Zyra's plant damage and the knock-up from Zyra R Stranglethorns can follow. Move sideways at the edge of its range to dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots as it travels in a straight line. When you see the indicator for Zyra R Stranglethorns, walk out of its area immediately.
Zyra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Zyra's magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots and build magic resistance.
Zyra.laning: Save at least one turret charge so you can place a turret immediately where a fight breaks out. After dodging the ability Zyra uses to grow a seed, step on the seed to destroy it.
Zyra.combo: While your fully charged turrets are firing, hit Zyra with Heimerdinger W Hextech Micro-Rockets and basic attacks to draw your turrets' fire onto her.
Zyra.escape: The moment you dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots to the side and bait it out is your chance to close the distance.
Zyra.phase: In the late game, your turrets can't keep up in a moving skirmish, so draw the fight to a spot you chose in advance.
